action_opcodes.name: EventStartPacket
action_opcodes.role: Generic event/command frame; carries combat intent via eventName + luaParams. Per client-architecture '1.x combat is asymmetric', this is the universal c2s combat-action carrier in 1.x: a player attack/cast/ability becomes an EventStart with the command identifier encoded in the event name/params, not via a dedicated opcode-per-action.

action_opcodes.name: PlayAnimationOnActorPacket
action_opcodes.role: Trigger an animation on a specific actor by animation ID. Payload is a single u64 (animationID).
action_opcodes.dispatchClassification: Pattern B (Actor cluster vftable[9]) per client-architecture 'S2C dispatch has five architectural patterns'. Opcode 0xDA falls inside 0xD3..0xE5 range. The actor-vftable9-investigation pass empirically proved all 95 RTTI-named actor classes route slot 9 to either AddReferenceResourceListener (BCS-Y-0529, the 19-class plurality), a no-op stub (BCS-Y-0528 / BCS-Y-0537), a Cut::Scheduler bool getter (BCS-Y-0536), or __purecall. NONE process opcode dispatch. The s2c PlayAnimationOnActor packet is therefore EITHER (a) processed via a parallel client-prediction system that reads the actor map at zone+0x17804 asynchronously, or (b) is processed by FUN_004D8860 sub-dispatch cases not yet enumerated for 0xDA.
action_opcodes.openQuestion: Whether 0xDA reaches CharaActionController via Pattern D sub-dispatchers. The pattern-d-subdispatcher pass enumerated FUN_004D8860 cases but the 0xDA opcode is not in its case table (0xCC/0xCD/0x12E..); FUN_0058CCA0 (the third router) handles 0xCC..0xE5 directly per its decomp note but the per-opcode disposition for 0xDA is not yet documented. live capture (deferred) or per-case enumeration of FUN_0058CCA0 would resolve.

action_opcodes.name: SetActorPropertyPacket
action_opcodes.role: Per-actor work-field property stream (Murmur2-hashed property ids). Combat-adjacent: carries state mutations including stats touched by combat (HP/MP/TP via property-id stream). Per combat_damage_findings.json: 'SetActorProperty 0x0137 remains the main actor-state mutation path' while CommandResult/BattleAction carries visual/numeric feedback.

action_opcodes.name: CommandResultX01Packet
action_opcodes.role: Single-target battle-result row. Wire payload: sourceActorId, animationId, commandId, magic 0x810, then one row with targetId + amount + worldMasterTextId + effectId + param + hitNum.

action_opcodes.name: CommandResultX10Packet / BattleActionX10Packet
action_opcodes.role: Up-to-10-target battle-result rows. Sparse SoA layout: targets@0x28, amounts@0x50, textIds@0x64, effectIds@0x78, params@0xA0, hitNums@0xAA.

action_opcodes.name: CommandResultX18Packet / BattleActionX18Packet
action_opcodes.role: Up-to-18-target battle-result rows (largest container variant). targets@0x28, amounts@0x70, textIds@0x94, effectIds@0xB8, params@0x100, hitNums@0x112.
action_opcodes.note: No pcap evidence in the 54-capture corpus; reached the 18-target shape only in large-group raid scenarios not captured. Static decomp coverage is complete.

action_opcodes.name: CommandResultX00Packet
action_opcodes.role: Zero-target battle-result (animation-only; no per-target damage rows). Used for casts that produce no numeric output (e.g. Disengage 12002, certain buffs).

c2s_0x012D_emitter.payloadStruct: BCS-S-0034 MapEventStartPayload (216 bytes total; 16-byte gameMessage header + 200-byte record). Fields: triggerActorId, ownerActorId, serverCodes/actionOrAbilityId, secondaryArgument, eventType, eventNamePrefix (32 bytes), luaParamBlob (128 bytes).
c2s_0x012D_emitter.architecturalNote: Per docs/client-architecture.md, '1.x combat is asymmetric'. The evidenced command-event path rides the generic EventStart 0x012D frame, and combat captures contain that envelope. The static route does not prove that every action kind uses it or expose a stable scalar gameCommand id; command-specific meaning remains in the event arguments, inline bytes, and Lua tail behind dynamic dispatch. The s2c display side uses dedicated CommandResult* opcodes (0x0139..0x013C). CharaActionController is NOT the c2s sender (BCS-Y-0434 verified no xrefs to FUN_00776760 or any sibling builder); it is receive-side playback infrastructure.

action_animation_chain_summary.actorVtableMethods_connection: The 'actor vtable method' that handles incoming action animations is CharaActionController slot 3 (FUN_00845430, BCS-Y-0434). This is a TICK method (the combat-action-c2s-findings pass established it iterates the 26 queue buckets at this+0x10 and invokes queued-object virtual slots at +0x08/+0x0C/+0x10/+0x14/+0x2C/+0x30, mutating per-item state 0/1/2/3). So CharaActionController.update DRIVES the queued actions every tick - but the QUEUE POPULATION mechanism (i.e. who calls CharaActionQue::enqueue from a packet handler) is what's missing from the catalog. The most likely hypothesis is that the BattleResult queue subsystem (BCS-Y-0412 ring buffer at FUN_005901D0) feeds the CharaActionController queue indirectly via the Vfx parameter path (BCS-Y-0417/0420), but this hop is not directly traced.
action_animation_chain_summary.predictedHypothesis: The full animation chain in 1.23b is likely: (s2c CommandResult 0x0139/0x013A/0x013B/0x013C arrives) -> staged into BattleResultQueueEntry ring buffer -> VfxRaptureParameter built -> RaptureActionDamageCallClip enqueued in CDev cut/scheduler -> clip Begin calls into CharaActor's CharaActionController.enqueue (via a pointer stored at some CharaActor field) -> CharaActionController.update tick (FUN_00845430) dispatches enqueued actions through CharaActionMotionController for skeletal animation and CharaActionVisual for VFX. The PlayAnimationOnActor 0x00DA opcode is likely a SEPARATE path for non-combat animations (emotes already have ActorDoEmote 0x00E1; 0x00DA may be for stage/event-driven animations triggered without a CommandResult preceeding). Confirmation requires either (i) decomp of FUN_0058CCA0 case 0xDA, or (ii) reverse-tracing from CharaActionController.enqueue (the vtable slot in CharaActionQue not yet identified) to find its callers.

proposed_bcs_y_entries.name: action_skill_subsystem_synthesis
proposed_bcs_y_entries.summary: The action/skill opcode family in FFXIV 1.23b is bifurcated: (a) c2s combat intent rides EventStart 0x012D (BCS-Y-0426 + client-architecture '1.x combat is asymmetric'); (b) s2c numeric/visual feedback uses CommandResult/BattleAction opcodes 0x0139/0x013A/0x013B/0x013C dispatched via FUN_0058CCA0 (BCS-Y-0404) into the BattleResultQueueEntry (BCS-S-0031) -> VfxRaptureParameter -> Rapture*Clip chain (fully cataloged BCS-Y-0405..0420); (c) the s2c actor animation trigger PlayAnimationOnActor 0x00DA falls in Pattern B Actor cluster range but the actor-vftable9-investigation pass proved no actor class processes opcodes via vftable[9] - the actual dispatch path is undocumented. The CharaAction* RTTI family (BCS-Y-0052..0058) is the receive-side action playback infrastructure (CharaActionController orchestrates; CharaActionMotionController plays skeletal motion; CharaActionVisual renders mesh/VFX) but the wire-packet to CharaActionController.enqueue link is not yet directly traced. The c2s 0x012D EventStart builder + wrappers are fully cataloged across BCS-Y-0426..0434.
proposed_bcs_y_entries.rationale: This manifest is pure synthesis - all material referenced is already in symbols.json. No new Ghidra runs were performed. Cataloging this as a finding (not a structural Y entry) so the action/skill subsystem can be cited from a single index entry rather than reconstructing from 13 scattered BCS-Y references plus client-architecture '1.x combat is asymmetric' + client-architecture 'S2C dispatch has five architectural patterns'.

proposed_bcs_y_entries.name: PlayAnimationOnActor_0x00DA_dispatch_path_open_question
proposed_bcs_y_entries.summary: Opcode 0x00DA (PlayAnimationOnActor, 31 pcap hits) is in the Pattern B Actor cluster range (0xD3..0xE5). The actor-vftable9-investigation pass empirically proved actor->vftable[9] is a no-op for every actor class - so the documented Pattern B dispatch cannot be doing the animation work. Three hypotheses remain: (a) the central dispatcher FUN_004DC690 has an earlier 0xDA case not yet enumerated (the low-switch-remaining-cases pass covered cases 0x03..0x0E + 0xCA/0xCB but not 0xDA); (b) the third-router FUN_0058CCA0 (per BCS-Y-0404 'cases handled directly: ... 0xCC..0xE5') may have a 0xDA-specific case routing to an animation-trigger function not yet linked to CharaActionController; (c) the packet is recorded into the actor map at zone+0x17804 and a parallel polling system applies it. Resolving requires either re-decomp of FUN_0058CCA0 (focus case 0xDA) or live capture (deferred indefinitely).
proposed_bcs_y_entries.rationale: Documents a specific gap so future phases don't re-investigate Pattern B for this opcode. The empirical no-op finding from the actor-vftable9-investigation pass is load-bearing for understanding why 'follow the vftable[9] dispatch' returns nothing useful here.

proposed_bcs_y_entries.name: CharaActionController_enqueue_caller_chain_open_question
proposed_bcs_y_entries.summary: The CharaAction* RTTI family (BCS-Y-0052..0058) is fully cataloged as RTTI. The pipeline is documented in docs/actor_action.md: PreLoadQue -> ActionQue.enqueue -> ActionController.update tick (BCS-Y-0434 slot 3) -> MotionController + ActionVisual. But the SPECIFIC vtable slot in CharaActionQue/CharaActionQueBase that implements ENQUEUE, and its callers, are not yet identified. Without this, the wire-packet -> CharaActionController link is missing. Most-likely candidates: (a) one of the 14 base or 26 multi-inheritance slots on CharaActionQue is the enqueue entrypoint; (b) it is called from the VfxRaptureClipProcessor (BCS-Y-0420) clip-Begin slot as part of the battle-result-to-animation hop; (c) it is called from a Pattern D sub-dispatcher case body. Resolution: enumerate xrefs to each CharaActionQue vtable slot via Ghidra, look for callers in the FUN_004DC690 / FUN_0058CCA0 / FUN_007C7F80 / FUN_00812B50 cluster.
proposed_bcs_y_entries.rationale: Frames the next-natural follow-up if action subsystem completeness becomes a priority. Doesn't propose any specific Ghidra work right now (per the no-symbols-edit phase constraint) - just records the gap with a concrete resolution path.

key_findings.title: Action/skill subsystem is already extensively cataloged
key_findings.detail: The action-skill-subsystem pass is dominantly a synthesis phase. Of the 7 combat-related opcodes (0x012D c2s, 0x0137/0x0139/0x013A/0x013B/0x013C/0x00DA s2c), 6 are fully cataloged across BCS-Y-0279/0404..0416/0426..0434 + BCS-S-0031/0034 + the actor-vftable9-investigation pass's vftable[9] empirical scan. The one not fully cataloged is the dispatch path of s2c 0x00DA PlayAnimationOnActor, which is documented as 'falls in Pattern B Actor cluster range but Pattern B is empirically a no-op' - an OPEN QUESTION with a clear next-step rather than a coverage gap.
key_findings.implication: The action-skill-subsystem pass produces 0 new BCS-Y catalog entries proper. The 3 proposed entries (0539 synthesis, 0540/0541 open questions) are all knowledge-organization entries rather than new code attributions.

key_findings.title: c2s 0x012D EventStart is the evidenced generic command-event carrier
key_findings.detail: Combat scenarios contain the 0x012D EventStart frame, and the preserved PlayerBaseClass._onCommandEvent path reaches _callServerOnCommand_cpp -> FUN_006EE680 (BCS-Y-0433) -> FUN_0075E3A0 -> FUN_00776760. The same opcode also occurs in many noncombat scenarios. Static evidence therefore proves the generic command-event route, not that every auto-attack, weaponskill, ability, and item use shares one fully decoded scalar schema.
key_findings.implication: Do not expect an opcode-per-action model, but also do not claim a stable gameCommand id field. The exact command mapping remains behind event arguments, inline bytes, the Lua parameter tail, and command-specific dynamic dispatch.

key_findings.title: s2c CommandResult/BattleAction family has 4 size variants for 0/1/10/18 target rows
key_findings.detail: The four opcodes 0x0139/0x013A/0x013B/0x013C are not different combat semantics but different SIZE BUCKETS for the same battle-result wire shape: X00 (0x013C, 0x48 bytes, 0 targets - animation only), X01 (0x0139, 0x58 bytes, 1 target), X10 (0x013A, 0xD8 bytes, up to 10 targets), X18 (0x013B, 0x148 bytes, up to 18 targets). All four route through the same FUN_0058CCA0 third-router, share the same BCS-S-0031 BattleResultQueueEntry (0x1A0 bytes), and the same downstream consumer FUN_007C7F80 (BCS-Y-0417). The server picks the smallest bucket that fits the action's target count - 0x013B (18-target) shows 0 pcap hits in the 54-capture corpus because no captured scenario had >10 targets in a single command result.
key_findings.implication: Server implementation can pick variants based on hit count without changing semantics. The X18 variant is correctly cataloged from decomp even without pcap evidence.

key_findings.title: Animation playback path: s2c packet -> CharaActionController is NOT yet directly traced
key_findings.detail: The CharaAction* RTTI class family is cataloged (BCS-Y-0052..0058) and its internal pipeline is well-documented (docs/actor_action.md). The CharaActionController slot 3 tick function (BCS-Y-0434 FUN_00845430) drives the action queue every tick. BUT the wire-packet to CharaActionController.enqueue link is the missing hop. Best-current-hypothesis (un-traced): BattleResult queue subsystem -> Vfx parameter -> RaptureActionDamageCallClip -> clip-Begin invokes CharaActionController via a vtable indirect call. Confirming this requires Ghidra xref enumeration of CharaActionQue's enqueue slot, which a work-pool item deferred under 'CharaActor stores pointers, not inline objects - the storage offset is TBD'.
key_findings.implication: Animation playback rendering is the LAST architectural gap in the combat receive path. Resolution is a focused 2-step Ghidra task (enumerate CharaActionQue vtable slot 'enqueue' xrefs; correlate with the BattleResult consumer chain) deferrable but not blocking server-side combat work.

key_findings.title: PlayAnimationOnActor 0x00DA is the only combat-adjacent opcode without a documented dispatch path
key_findings.detail: Per opcode dispatch table: 0x00DA falls in the Actor cluster 0xD3..0xE5 range; Pattern B dispatch (actor->vftable[9]) is empirically no-op per the actor-vftable9-investigation pass. The third-router FUN_0058CCA0's case list 'directly handles 0xCC..0xE5' per BCS-Y-0404 notes but specific case 0xDA's disposition is not enumerated. PCAP shows 31 hits so the opcode IS observed.
key_findings.implication: Open question recorded as proposed BCS-Y-0540. Either re-decomp FUN_0058CCA0 with focus on case 0xDA (cheap, static; can be done in a follow-up phase) or accept the gap and defer to live capture.
